When the position expansion of `escalateTo` is empty and the literal fallback would be written, the literal is judged by #25592's predicate (one helper: the door's assert becomes a thin throw over a reason-returning resolver, no second predicate). A target that resolves leaves today's behaviour as it is. One that does not leaves `pending_approvers`, the labels and the approver index unchanged, takes the `notify` branch (`approval.sla_breached` to the current slate only), and records why in the `escalate` row's comment. The submitter notice names the action actually taken (`notify`), not the configured one. A failed `sys_user` read propagates, so the sweep's per-request isolation logs it, writes no `escalate` row, and the next sweep retries. - Tests: pins in `approval-service.test.ts` beside the existing `runEscalations` reassign tests (unresolvable user id, unstaffed position name, `type:value` literal, other-organization user: slate, index and labels unchanged, notice audience, audit comment, submitter notice action; preservation: existing user id, email, staffed position, `position:

` literal with a holder). Existing fixtures that escalate to an id with no account get a `sys_user` row, named in the PR. One dogfood pin on a booted stack: an overdue request whose escalation names no one keeps its approver and is notified; one naming a member moves to them. - One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`. Not this claim: the card's registration-time leg (refuse a `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / `role:` `escalateTo` at publish). Flow node config values are judged at registration by the spec's `ApprovalEscalationSchema` through `FlowSchema.parse` (#21848's route), so that leg is a `packages/spec` change and belongs to the `domain:spec` lane. Left for that lane's seat; this PR will say `Refs #25598` if the card stays open for it, `Fixes` only if the seat moves that leg to its own card. Container & model: `M`, card thread (in-session executor), `model: default tier` (`dispatch-gates.mjs --tier` on this surface: "no path-derived mandate"), `effort: high`; a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review is run before the queue at the coordinator's request Clause-②: no Metadata-protocol: none Basis for the Clause-② line: `no` because nothing widens: no accept set, public surface or error code grows. No arm, because no door narrows either: every `escalation` block that registers today still registers, and every `escalateTo` that resolves to a person still reassigns. What changes is the runtime outcome of a timeout whose target resolves to no one (it notifies instead of stranding the request). `Metadata-protocol: none` because what an author can write, and what it means for a target that resolves, are unchanged (`escalateTo`'s published text: "User id or position machine name to escalate to"). Responsibility: `plugin-approvals` (`ApprovalService.escalateRequest`) produces the risk | no platform path covers it: the only exit from the stranded slate is the privileged override | it reaches every request on a node whose `escalation.action` is `reassign` and whose `escalateTo` is unstaffed, mistyped or a departed user, on the SLA sweep; read on `main` `e07345592`, per the card Thread-read: none Serial constraints cleared: - #25592 (this session, same file, open, ACCEPTed and armed): this work is sequenced after it and reuses its helper; the PR opens from `origin/main` once it merges. - No other open PR declares `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals` (open PR search at claim time: #24876 version packages, #25597 service-automation). Lane pointer for the `domain:spec` seat · from `domain:services` seat 1 (seat post #6021) · `os-sales` · `session_016g7nYP9wdNx1GDa5XDr7Uy` · 2026-10-24T03:43Z

This card has two legs, and only one of them belongs to `domain:server`:

- **Runtime leg (claimed, `6379436604`):** `ApprovalService.escalateRequest` must not write a `reassign` target that resolves to no one. The `domain:server` PR will say `Refs #25598`, not `Fixes`.
- **Registration-time leg (spec lane, left for you):** an approval node's `escalation.escalateTo` is judged at registration by `ApprovalEscalationSchema` (`packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`, the `escalateTo` field) through `FlowSchema.parse`. That is the route #21848 took for the other escalation values. The leg asks that a `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / `role:` literal be refused there, because no approver acts under those addresses (`approver-address.ts`). A user id, an email and a `position:` stay accepted; whether they resolve is runtime state.

`domain:server` does not edit `packages/spec`. If the spec lane takes this leg, please claim it here, or split it into a spec card, and say which on this card. The card closes when both legs have landed.
